biography.plain_text: Hubert Greinwalder helped professionalize Germany's fitness-club market. An architect by training, he opened a club near Munich in 1991 and co-founded Greinwalder & Partner, a marketing consultancy for fitness operators. He later became a shareholder and inventor in Airpressure Bodyforming, whose wearable exercise equipment is distributed through partner studios across Europe.

long_biography.plain_text:
A visit to conventional gyms prompted architect Hubert Greinwalder to imagine a more welcoming kind of exercise club. He left his architectural job and opened AKTIV HAUS in Freising in 1991, combining training with a substantial wellness area and a social setting. After working with INLINE, he and Oliver Sekula established Greinwalder & Partner in 1997. The firm advised clubs on marketing, sales and business development for many years.

Greinwalder subsequently pursued a product concept that applies alternating air pressure during workouts. The Airpressure Bodyforming venture subsequently developed equipment used by a European network of partner studios. He is named as a shareholder rather than the current managing director; patents for the devices list him among their inventors. This later work connects his experience with fitness customers and club operators to the design of exercise products. In an interview he described his break from the consultancy as a chance to travel before returning to the industry.
